bull.b: The large, long-duration Anthropic lease provides substantial contracted demand for TeraWulf’s AI infrastructure platform. Google credit support and Fluor’s expanded EPC role further strengthen financing and execution, improving the potential for contracted demand to convert into durable cash flow.

Rapid growth in HPC lease revenue indicates that TeraWulf is progressing beyond bitcoin mining toward infrastructure leasing with recurring revenue characteristics. Increasing the share of lease revenue can improve business-model durability as additional contracted capacity becomes operational.

Strong reported liquidity and expanded financing capacity give TeraWulf resources to fund construction, tenant commitments and near-term growth. Greater access to capital also supports execution of large projects while reducing immediate dependence on equity-market financing.

bear.b: Severe losses and sustained negative operating and free cash flow show that the business is not currently self-funding. Continued cash burn can require additional financing, constrain capital allocation and increase dilution or refinancing risk as TeraWulf expands its infrastructure.

Very high leverage relative to equity and substantial interest outflows reduce financial flexibility as project spending continues. A thin capital base leaves less capacity to absorb operating setbacks, while debt service can consume liquidity before new contracted capacity reaches revenue generation.

Scaling complex data-center projects while skilled electrical labor is constrained creates schedule and cost execution risk. The large gap between current reported and targeted HPC margins also indicates that tenant fit-out, development and pre-revenue costs may pressure profitability during the buildout period.
